title: Audit log transparency & customer commitments — draft language
content:
Purpose and context:
This doc is a working draft of customer-facing wording and internal talking points around audit-log coverage, retention, access models, and how those controls map to SOC2/ISO/HIPAA conversations. Goal: give Sales/CS a tight set of approved sentences + fallback phrasing for sensitive asks, and a short internal checklist for legal/engineering to lock down before final claims.

Status: draft; not yet approved by Legal or Security.

Executive summary (single paragraph):
Redwood provides detailed, tamper-evident audit logs for all request/response activity tied to customer accounts and keys, with configurable retention windows, searchable export, and role-based access controls. For customers requiring SOC2/ISO/HIPAA evidence, we offer exportable audit bundles and attestations tied to our compliance programs; for Private deployments we support local audit storage and direct ingestion into customer SIEM.

Core customer-facing pillars (short bullets for reps):
- Visibility: "We capture a detailed, immutable trail for each inference request — timestamps, model variant, route, latency, token counts, and operation metadata."
- Control: "Retention is configurable per-tenant (hosted) and fully customer-managed for Private deployments (VPC/on-prem)."
- Access & export: "Logs are searchable in Console, streamable to customer SIEM via S3/Kafka, and exportable as time-bound bundles for audits."
- Evidence: "Our SOC2/ISO artifacts include controls around log integrity, monitoring, and alerting; HIPAA customers get additional guidance on covered entity obligations and recommended configurations."

Recommended short claims (copyable):
- "Redwood maintains immutable audit logs containing request metadata and system events; customers can retain logs for up to X years (configurable)."
- "Audit logs are available in the Console, and can be replicated to your S3 or streaming endpoint for long-term retention and ingestion into your SIEM."
- "For Dedicated/Private deployments we can support customer-controlled log ingestion and key management so audit data never leaves your VPC."

Detailed claim language and mapping to compliance frameworks:
- SOC2: emphasize log integrity, access controls, monitoring, and retention. Suggested phrasing: "As part of our SOC2 program, we collect and retain audit logs that demonstrate control operation, access patterns, and system changes. Logs are integrity-protected and monitored for anomalies as part of our security operations."
- ISO27001: emphasize information security management and evidence for Annex A controls. Phrasing: "We maintain audit trails and change histories that support ISO27001 control objectives; customers can request scoped evidence related to logging and monitoring controls."
- HIPAA: be conservative — avoid overclaiming. Phrasing: "Redwood supports customers in meeting HIPAA logging and access monitoring requirements by providing detailed audit logs and tooling to export logs. Customers remain responsible for mapping these artifacts to their HIPAA documentation and workflows. We offer Private deployment options for customers requiring full data sovereignty."

Examples: what to show in the Console (for demo):
- Per-request row: request_id, timestamp, customer_id, route/model, latency_ms, token_count_in, token_count_out, response_status, policy_flag (if any), KV cache hit/miss, backend instance id (redacted for hosted shared infra if needed).
- Search filters: time range, customer id, model, route, status code, error type, policy flag, request metadata tag.
- Exports: zipped NDJSON bundle with manifest + signature.

Language to avoid / risky claims (legal should vet):
- "We anonymize and never store inputs" — avoid unless proven for all modes and explicit retention windows.
- "HIPAA-covered" as a blanket term — instead say "we support HIPAA compliance" and clarify customer obligations.
- "Immutable" without definition — say "tamper-evident" or "integrity-protected" and specify mechanisms (checksums, append-only storage).

Competitive differentiation (talking points vs X/Y/Z competitors):
- vs large cloud-managed LLMs: emphasize ability to deliver export-ready audit bundles and higher fidelity logs tied to model variant and token-level metrics (many competitors only provide basic request-level logs).
- vs self-hosted runtimes: Redwood offers the hybrid story — hosted convenience + private deployment parity for audit controls, plus standard integrations to SIEM and compliance artifacts to accelerate procurement.
- vs inference platforms that throttle evidence: pitch our Console search + streaming hooks and suggest a quick POC: "we can stream a week of logs to your SIEM to validate ingestion and alerting."

Quick FAQ for Sales (short answers to common red flags):
Q: "Can you give us raw request/response content for PII review?"
A: "We can provide log bundles containing request metadata and, where retention rules permit, full request/response payloads. For hosted customers we recommend a scoped export or Private deployment if continuous access to payloads is required. All exports are access-controlled and logged."

Q: "How long are logs kept?"
A: "Default retention is 90 days in hosted; configurable up to X years for enterprise contracts and unlimited for Private deployments under customer control."

Q: "Are logs tamper-proof?"
A: "We protect log integrity with append-only storage and cryptographic checksums. Export bundles include a signed manifest for audit verification."

Implementation notes / TODOs for engineering/security before sign-off:
- Confirm exact default retention numbers and enterprise max (fill X).
- Document mechanisms: append-only store, checksum algorithm, signing key rotation cadence, and who holds keys (Redwood vs customer KMS).
- Validate export format (NDJSON manifest schema) and update Console screenshots used in customer collateral.
- Legal: approve HIPAA phrasing, map claims to evidence artifacts in compliance evidence library.
- Build an internal playbook for on-prem/Private export workflow to support sales demos.

Sales enablement snippets (quick soundbites):
- "Export-ready audit bundles, streaming to your SIEM in under an hour."
- "Configurable retention and VPC-first options for customers who need full custody of logs."
- "Signed manifests and checksums mean you can present tamper-evidence in audits without custom tooling."

Open questions (needs answers before finalizing):
- Who is the canonical owner for the signed-manifest keys? Security or Customer (for Hosted vs Private)?
- What is the maximum enterprise retention we will offer for hosted (tech and cost implications)?
- Do we provide an API for programmatic export of bundles or only Console + manual export?
- What's the recommended wording for cross-account sharing of logs with third-party auditors?

Appendix: suggested export manifest outline (high level, for legal/engineering):
- bundle_id, generated_at, retention_policy, customer_id, manifest_hash, files: [request_logs.ndjson, system_events.ndjson], signature: <base64>
(note: detailed schema tracked in Confluence link above)

Internal notes / scratch (unpolished):
- demo idea: spin a 24hr log stream into Splunk during EBC and show live alerting on anomaly detection (cost: small infra PR).
- small ask to engineering: add model_variant field to audit rows if not present — critical for customers who A/B test models.
- incomplete: needs example signed manifest + sample NDJSON for legal review.

Next steps (owner/ETA):
- Legal review of phrasing (owner: Priya) — due 2026-02-05
- Engineering confirm retention/integrity mechanics (owner: Jonas) — due 2026-01-30
- Draft final one-pager and Console screenshots for Sales kit (owner: Maya) — due 2026-02-12

End of draft.
notes: Working doc intended for go-to-market and security alignment; contains TODOs and unresolved items. Do not publish externally until Legal and Security sign-off.
